text: The in-game Radahn Festival event allows players to summon multiple NPC allies, such as Blaidd and Alexander, representing his soldiers' way of honoring him with a worthy final battle.
In her boss fight, Malenia heals from every hit she lands on the player, even through guard, draining the player's vitality and reflecting her lifelong survival philosophy of aggression as defense.
The fight against Placidusax is accessed by lying down among ancient bones arranged in a circle as a ritual invitation.
The fight against Fortissax is accessed through Fia's questline in the deathbed dream, retrieving the Cursemark of Death.
Defeating Maliketh releases the Rune of Death back into the world, allowing destined death to return and making the previously golden-thorn-sealed Erdtree penetrable for the final stages of the game.
Sorcery in Elden Ring's mythology draws power from glintstone, crystallized cosmic starlight, making it a source of power independent of the Erdtree.
The Mimic Tear takes on the player character's appearance, weapons, armor, and spells, fighting as an exact copy of the player without their consciousness or history.
The fog gate is interpreted as a threshold of attention, separating the ordinary world from a story the game has been saving, requiring commitment to enter and encounter it fully.
Crucible-referencing incantations let the caster temporarily manifest animalistic traits such as tails, wings, or armored carapaces, echoing the primordial blending of life.
Under the Golden Order, ordinary people did not truly die; their spirits returned to the Erdtree through underground catacombs to be sustained or sent back.
Demigods and lords under the Golden Order could be killed in battle but could not permanently die, due to the removal of the Rune of Death.
Grace can call to Tarnished descendants generations later even if they have no direct memory of the original promise, drawing them back to the Lands Between.
Tarnished who die can be revived repeatedly by the grace that resurrects them, allowing effectively unlimited deaths and returns.
The game describes the power of the Great Runes as a 'mad taint' rather than a pure gift, amplifying each demigod's existing traits.
The grace light from the Erdtree now appears only as thin, faint Sites of Grace guiding tarnished, remnants of a nearly depleted divine power.
Malenia can bloom a smaller version of the Scarlet Aeonia during battle, filling the arena with rot.
The Tarnished receives a call in the form of a golden guiding thread of grace that leads toward the Erdtree, promising the chance to restore the Elden Ring and become Elden Lord.
The Tarnished consumes Great Runes taken from fallen demigods over the course of the journey.
The Sites of Grace are depicted narratively as fragments of the Erdtree's fading grace and the world's memory of what it was meant to be.
Each Site of Grace points in a direction suggesting where the player should go next, but players can choose to ignore this guidance and explore elsewhere.
It is implied that warrior jars absorb the essence and martial prowess of the fallen warriors they consume.
Before being granted an audience with Rykard and joining the family, newly recruited Tarnished must invade fellow Tarnished to prove their resolve.
Leda urges the player to touch the withered arm, a portal to the Realm of Shadow where Miquella resides.
Dryleaf Dane's fighting style, Dane's Footwork, emphasizes powerful and precise kicks developed through training under a waterfall.
